newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise to be short-lived.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise to be short-lived.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Wednesday, but traders said the fall which started in the second half of the day would continue on Thursday.
The Russian Trading System index of 23 shares edged up by 2.54 percent to 298.81 on $38.39 million on total market volume.
Traders said that Russian operators optimism over a rise in Dow Jones index did not find enough support from investors and some shares closed at Tuesday's closing levels.
The Dow Jones industrial average ended with a gain of 135.26 points, or 2.10 percent, at 6,587.16 on Tuesday, propelled by positive news on retail inflation.
"Clients' money in no way supported the rise," said a Western bank trader, "As soon as U.S. long bonds started falling, Russia was kicked down too."
Alexei Abdurakhimov, chief trader at IFCI-Moscow Partners said Western buying would be "quiet and unaggressive", adding that no serious Western money would come before May.
"It is our Russian speculator who is worrying, as he understands the rise was a game," he said. "That's why we shall fall again tomorrow, at least in the first half of the day."
But the Western bank trader said he did not expect a strong fall in the next few days, but said that there could be a nosedive in May.
National power utility UES ordinaries rose to $0.2188 from $0.2135 at Tuesday's close, LUKoil edged up to $13.58 from $13.40.
